clue.text: Disperse liquid in small dish

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Someone spills a little liquid into a small dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter is to splash or spray drops of a fluid about, scattering it.

clue.text: Try politician in North West town

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the name of the town

parts.note: Sale is a town near Manchester in North West England
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician being tried in a northern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample is to taste or test a little of something.

clue.text: Nymphs line a rave dancing?

indicators.note: dancing jumbles the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Woodland nymphs queuing up for a rave and dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nymphs' suggests mythological maidens, but it means immature insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is the immature form of some insects, like a grub or maggot.

clue.text: After time register one living under bridge?

indicators.note: after puts the register word after the time letter

parts.note: a roll is a register of names

explanation.surface: Someone takes a register after a while for a person living under a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In folk tales a monstrous creature lurks beneath a bridge, as in the Billy Goats Gruff.

clue.text: Precisely perform first two parts of lyric by former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
to act is to perform

indicators.note: the first two parts of the word means its opening two letters

explanation.surface: An ex sings the first two verses of a song exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly and precisely both mean without any error or deviation.

clue.text: Prisoner and scoundrel agree

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
a cur is a contemptible, worthless man

explanation.surface: A convict and a villain reach an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Exaggerate deliveries going to art gallery

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain

explanation.surface: Deliveries heading to an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a cricket term: six balls bowled in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to claim more than is true, to exaggerate.

clue.text: Clergyman in church by a prairie

parts.note: a prairie is a broad grassy plain

explanation.surface: A minister in church next to a stretch of grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman serving an institution such as a school or regiment.

clue.text: Approximate time to produce fibre

parts.note: rough means approximate
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A roughly estimated time to produce fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is dietary fibre, the indigestible part of food.

clue.text: Plant officer eats right before a mass

indicators.note: the officer swallows the next letter, which goes inside the word

parts.note: a major is an army officer
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: An army officer dines on something just before attending Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic herb of the mint family, a garden plant.

clue.text: Initially dismiss everything just as very unusual and weird sensation

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to brush off everything as merely very odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the uncanny feeling of having already lived through the present moment.

clue.text: Decide against boxing plan

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the clue words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Making up one's mind to oppose a boxing scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intention, as in 'my idea is to leave early'.

clue.text: Distributed publicity material the French left during a fair day

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: during places the word for left inside the following run of letters

parts.note: a fete is a fair or gala

explanation.surface: A Frenchman departed while a fair was on, handing out flyers.
explanation.walkthrough: The L goes inside FETE, making A + FLETE + D.
explanation.definitionFit: To have leafleted an area is to have handed out printed handbills there.

clue.text: Be quiet about thickness returning in spirit

indicators.note: about tells us the hush word goes around the following letters

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: returning means the word for thickness is read backwards

parts.note: ply is a layer or strand, a measure of thickness in wool or plywood

explanation.surface: A call for silence about a thick layer coming back in a ghostly form.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is an imaginary airy being, an elemental spirit of the air.

clue.text: Dock is important to auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: An accountant considers a dock to be significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like a financial checker, but here it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone landing place where ships moor, a dock.

clue.text: Wound staunched without scars

indicators.note: read as the past of wind, wound means twisted, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: An injury whose bleeding stopped and left no scars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury but is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscathed means wholly unharmed, so bearing no marks of injury.

clue.text: Fantastic magazine distributed without energy

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters are spread around into a new order
without means the letter for energy is taken out

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A wonderful magazine handed out with no oomph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes E from MAGAZINE, leaving MAGAZIN, which 'distributed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing and fantastic are both loose terms of praise for something extraordinary.

clue.text: Rude sprite with tie to king

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
a rope is something to tie with
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An impolite fairy tying itself to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means indecent or unseemly, close to rude or vulgar.

clue.text: Slimy cop running in international competition

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move into a new order

explanation.surface: A slippery policeman running in a global event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympics are the Games where athletes of many nations compete.

clue.text: Agreement rejected after mother left drop of mulled wine

indicators.note: after puts the reversed agreement word behind the rest

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: a drop of something is a tiny amount, here just its first letter
rejected suggests turning back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Mother refused and walked off, leaving a little mulled wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmsey is a sweet fortified Madeira, a dessert wine.

clue.text: Talk about being embraced by ox

indicators.note: embraced means held inside, so the ox word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired ox of Tibet
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A conversation about being hugged by an ox.
explanation.definitionFit: To yack is to chatter idly at length, informal for talk.

clue.text: Work in the garden every other weekend

indicators.note: every other picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Gardening chores done on alternate weekends.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed is to pull unwanted plants from beds, a garden task.

clue.text: Hail desirable reception

definitions.meaning: to hail someone is to greet them warmly
as an adjective the word means pleasing, gladly received
as a noun the word means a greeting given to a guest

explanation.surface: Hailing a much-wanted reception.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as verb (greet), adjective (pleasing) and noun (greeting).

clue.text: Nerve to drop ball for a contest

indicators.note: dropping one letter means it is taken out and replaced by another
for means in exchange, as the new letter goes in

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: Losing your nerve and dropping the ball in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE, British slang for nerve, swaps its O for an A.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight or struggle, a contest.

clue.text: Remove frost around head of vital instrument

indicators.note: around means the defrosting word is placed round the letter

parts.note: to de-ice is to clear ice or frost

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Clearing ice from round the top of a vital piece of kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is a gadget, a tool or instrument.

clue.text: Unusual degree in dance

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A strange qualification in dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Devote attention to four consumed by religious sect

indicators.note: by places the sect beside the rest, here first

parts.note: a cult is a small religious group
IV is four in Roman numerals
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Four people swallowed up by a strange religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate a person or skill is to foster it with care and effort.

clue.text: Popular judge rises to conclude

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ref, a referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: A well-liked judge stands to sum up.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or draw a conclusion from evidence.

clue.text: Page with amusing predicament

parts.note: light reading or entertainment is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: A page boy in a funny fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a dangerous or difficult situation, a fix.

clue.text: Paper directed at recent union members

definitions.text: Paper directed at recent union members

parts.words: Paper directed at recent union members
parts.note: the recent union is a wedding: guests throw little paper shapes at the newlyweds

explanation.surface: A publication aimed at new trade union members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bits of coloured paper are showered over bride and groom after a wedding.

clue.text: Desire broadcast to be live

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A wish to go on air live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' looks like broadcasting jargon, but it is a verb meaning dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or make one's home there.

clue.text: Always returning to accept press release that's for Amnesty

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the reversed word holds the others
returning means the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always
PR is public relations, the business of press releases
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A recurring release to the press on behalf of Amnesty International.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EVER into REVE, which takes in PRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a cancellation or postponement of punishment, like a pardon.
